question:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error.

(A) Taylor, Richard, and / (B) Francis plays for / (C) the state / (D) basketball team.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. B.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject of the sentence is "Taylor, Richard, and Francis" — three persons joined by "and", which makes the subject plural. A plural subject takes the plural verb "play", not the singular "plays".

◦ Correct: Taylor, Richard, and Francis play for the state basketball team.

• Part (B) "Francis plays for" therefore contains the error, because the "-s" verb form has been wrongly used with a plural subject.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Part (A) "Taylor, Richard, and" — correct listing of the compound subject.

• Part (C) "the state" and Part (D) "basketball team" — both are correct; "state basketball team" is a proper noun phrase.

• Learners are often misled by the noun standing immediately before the verb ("Francis"), but the verb must agree with the whole subject, not with the nearest noun. This trap is called the proximity error.

NOTE

• Subject–verb agreement rules for SSC:

◦ Two or more subjects joined by "and" → plural verb (Ram and Shyam are here).

◦ But if the joined nouns refer to one person/thing, the verb is singular (Bread and butter is my breakfast; The poet and singer has arrived).

◦ Subjects joined by "or / nor / either...or / neither...nor" → the verb agrees with the nearer subject (Neither the boys nor the teacher was present).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Pay an arm and a leg for something
option_2: Pay a lot of money for something
option_3: Give a lot of love and care to someone
option_4: Pay a lot of attention to an incident
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Pay a lot of money for something.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to pay an arm and a leg for something" means to pay a very large amount of money for something; to find something extremely expensive. (किसी चीज़ के लिए बहुत ज़्यादा कीमत चुकाना)

◦ Example: We had to pay an arm and a leg for those concert tickets.

• The image behind the idiom is that the price is so high that one would have to give up a limb to afford it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Be devoted to unwanted things" and Option 3 "Give a lot of love and care to someone" wrongly read "arm and leg" as an expression of affection.

• Option 4 "Pay a lot of attention to an incident" confuses the phrase with "pay attention", which is a different collocation altogether.

NOTE

• Related money idioms often asked in SSC exams:

◦ "Cost a fortune / cost a bomb" — to be extremely expensive.

◦ "Break the bank" — to use up all one's money.

◦ "Foot the bill" — to pay for something.

◦ "Tighten one's belt" — to spend less because of shortage of money.

◦ "Make ends meet" — to earn just enough to cover expenses.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

As they driven through the dark, twisting lane / down which they had walked earlier, Lucius heard / the whistling of the night air in his ears.
option_1: down which they had walked earlier, Lucius heard
option_3: the whistling of the night air in his ears.
option_4: As they driven through the dark, twisting lane
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. As they driven through the dark, twisting lane.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The clause needs a finite verb in the simple past tense, but the sentence wrongly uses the past participle (V3) "driven" without any auxiliary verb.

• The verb "drive" forms: drive – drove (V2) – driven (V3). Since the action is a completed past action running parallel with "Lucius heard", the correct form is the simple past "drove".

◦ Correct: As they drove through the dark, twisting lane down which they had walked earlier, Lucius heard the whistling of the night air in his ears.

• "Driven" could be used only with an auxiliary — "had driven", "were driven", "have driven" — none of which is present here.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Part 1 "down which they had walked earlier, Lucius heard" is correct: the past perfect "had walked" rightly shows the earlier of two past actions, and "down which" is the correct relative structure.

• Part 3 "the whistling of the night air in his ears." is correct — "the whistling of ... in his ears" is idiomatic.

NOTE

• Never use V3 (past participle) alone as the main verb of a clause. Common SSC traps: "He gone (× ) → He went", "She written (× ) → She wrote", "They taken (× ) → They took".

• Irregular verb table to revise: go–went–gone, write–wrote–written, drive–drove–driven, take–took–taken, ring–rang–rung, sing–sang–sung.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Trivial
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Minor.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Trivial" (adjective) means of little value or importance; insignificant; petty. Its closest synonym here is "minor", which also means small, lesser or unimportant. (तुच्छ / महत्वहीन)

◦ Example: Do not waste time quarrelling over such a trivial / minor matter.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Fatal" means causing death or disaster — an antonym in force (a fatal issue is anything but trivial).

• Option 3 "Decisive" means settling an issue conclusively; very important — again the opposite of trivial.

• Option 4 "Formal" means official or according to convention, which is unrelated to importance.

NOTE

• Synonyms of trivial: minor, petty, insignificant, trifling, negligible, frivolous, paltry.

• Antonyms of trivial: important, significant, vital, crucial, momentous, weighty.

• Related word family: trivia (unimportant details), trivialise (to make something seem less important than it is).

question:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.

Ministry of education has announced that students can ________ the Board Examinations twice.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. take.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In standard English the fixed collocation is "take an examination" (also "sit for an examination" / "appear for an examination"), meaning to write/attempt the exam as a candidate. (परीक्षा देना)

◦ Correct: ... students can take the Board Examinations twice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "participate" needs the preposition "in" (participate in a competition) and is not used with examinations.

• Option 3 "give an exam" is common Indian colloquial usage but is non-standard; in correct English the teacher/board gives an exam and the student takes it.

• Option 4 "get the examination" is meaningless; one "gets" a result, not an examination.

NOTE

• Useful examination collocations: take / sit (for) / appear for / attempt an exam; pass, clear, crack, fail, retake an exam; set, conduct, invigilate, evaluate an exam.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.

A man of character, he stuck to his guns even in the most difficult situations.
option_1: To do things that would please people
option_4: To stand firm against all difficulties and challenges
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. To stand firm against all difficulties and challenges.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to stick to one's guns" means to refuse to change one's opinion or course of action despite opposition, criticism or difficulty; to stand firm. (अपनी बात पर अड़े रहना / दृढ़ रहना)

◦ Example: Though everyone opposed the plan, the manager stuck to his guns and it finally succeeded.

• The context "A man of character ... even in the most difficult situations" clearly supports the sense of firmness and steadfastness.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "To do things that would please people" is the sense of "to curry favour" / "to butter someone up" — the very opposite of standing firm.

• Option 2 "To behave disrespectfully" has no link with the idiom.

• Option 3 "To find a treasure" wrongly takes the idiom literally.

NOTE

• Idioms of firmness and determination: "stand one's ground", "hold one's own", "put one's foot down", "stick to one's guns", "leave no stone unturned".

• Idioms of yielding: "back down", "give in", "throw in the towel", "toe the line".

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined segment in the given sentence.

After her husband passed away, Jane had to learn to bite the bullet and take care of the household on her own.
option_4: Run away from a difficult situation
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Accept a difficult situation bravely.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to bite the bullet" means to face a painful or unpleasant situation with courage; to endure hardship bravely because it cannot be avoided. (कठिनाई को साहस के साथ सहना)

◦ Example: With prices rising, the family had to bite the bullet and cut down its expenses.

• Origin: before anaesthetics, wounded soldiers were made to bite on a bullet to bear the pain of surgery — hence the sense of enduring pain bravely.

• The context — a widow taking charge of the household alone — fits this meaning perfectly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Create a difficult situation" reverses the sense: the idiom is about facing, not creating, hardship.

• Option 3 "Criticise someone harshly" is the meaning of idioms like "pull someone to pieces" or "take someone to task".

• Option 4 "Run away from a difficult situation" is the exact opposite — that would be "to chicken out" or "to beat a retreat".

NOTE

• Similar idioms of endurance: "face the music" (accept the unpleasant consequences), "grin and bear it", "weather the storm", "keep a stiff upper lip", "take it on the chin".

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given phrase.

One who lends money to others at a very high rate of interest.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Usurer.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "usurer" is a person who lends money at an unreasonably or illegally high rate of interest. The practice itself is called "usury". (सूदखोर / ब्याजखोर)

◦ Example: Poor farmers often fall into the clutches of village usurers.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Curator" — a person in charge of a museum, art gallery or library collection.

• Option 2 "Bankrupt" — a person officially declared unable to pay his debts (insolvent).

• Option 4 "Numismatist" — a person who studies or collects coins and medals.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes frequently asked in SSC:

◦ Philatelist — one who collects postage stamps.

◦ Connoisseur — an expert judge in matters of taste (especially art).

◦ Miser — one who hoards wealth and spends as little as possible.

◦ Creditor — one to whom money is owed; Debtor — one who owes money.

◦ Broker — an agent who buys and sells on behalf of others.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

The platinum is a precious metal.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The platinum.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Platinum" is a material (uncountable) noun used here in a general sense, and material nouns used generally do not take the definite article "the".

◦ Correct: Platinum is a precious metal.

• The article "the" would be used only if the noun were particularised — e.g., "The platinum used in this ring is of high purity."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "is" is correct: an uncountable/material noun takes a singular verb.

• Option 3 "a" is correct before the singular countable noun phrase "precious metal" beginning with a consonant sound.

• Option 4 "precious metal" is a correct and idiomatic noun phrase.

NOTE

• Rules on the omission of "the" (very common in SSC):

◦ Before material nouns used generally — Gold is costly. Water is essential.

◦ Before abstract nouns used generally — Honesty is the best policy.

◦ Before proper nouns, languages, meals, subjects, games — English, breakfast, physics, cricket.

◦ But "the" IS used with rivers, seas, oceans, mountain ranges, holy books, newspapers and superlatives — the Ganga, the Himalayas, the Gita, the best.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

All praised him when he soared in the business world, but the same people ______ him when he failed in business.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. criticised.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence is built on a contrast signalled by "but" and "the same people": people first "praised" him in success, so in failure they must have done the opposite — "criticised" him (found fault with him). (आलोचना करना)

◦ Correct: All praised him when he soared in the business world, but the same people criticised him when he failed in business.

• "Praised" and "criticised" form a natural antonym pair, which is exactly what the contrast demands.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "nourished" (fed / nurtured) does not contrast with "praised".

• Option 3 "supported" is a synonym of the positive attitude, so it destroys the contrast.

• Option 4 "dramatised" (presented in a dramatic manner) is contextually meaningless here.

NOTE

• In "fill in the blank" items, first locate the signal word: "but, however, although, whereas, yet, on the contrary" demand a contrasting word, while "and, moreover, besides, similarly" demand a similar word.

• Synonyms of criticise: censure, condemn, denounce, disparage, reproach, find fault with.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

What most off us want most is to move forward.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. most off.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The intended expression is "most of us" (a quantifier + "of" + pronoun). The sentence wrongly writes "off" (with a double "f") in place of the preposition "of".

◦ Correct: What most of us want most is to move forward.

• "Of" is a preposition showing part of a group — most of us, many of them, some of the boys.

• "Off" is an adverb/preposition meaning "away from", "removed from" — He fell off the ladder; Switch off the fan.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "is to" is correct — the singular verb "is" agrees with the noun clause subject "What most of us want most", and it is followed by the to-infinitive "to move".

• Option 3 "want most" is correct — the adverb "most" (to the greatest degree) rightly qualifies "want".

• Option 4 "move forward" is correct — "forward" is the standard adverb of direction.

NOTE

• Frequently confused pairs of this type in SSC papers: of / off, quite / quiet, loose / lose, advice / advise, affect / effect, principal / principle, stationary / stationery, accept / except.

question:
Select the word which means the same as the group of words given.

That which can’t be read.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Illegible.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Illegible" means not clear enough to be read; impossible to decipher (usually of handwriting or print). (अपठनीय)

◦ Example: The doctor's prescription was completely illegible.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Inaccessible" — that which cannot be reached or approached.

• Option 2 "Incurable" — a disease that cannot be cured.

• Option 4 "Irrelevant" — not connected with or not applicable to the matter in hand.

NOTE

• Do not confuse "illegible" (cannot be read because of bad writing) with "ineligible" (not qualified/entitled) — a very common SSC trap.

• Related one-word substitutes: legible (clear enough to read), indelible (that cannot be erased), inaudible (that cannot be heard), invisible (that cannot be seen), incorrigible (that cannot be corrected/reformed), inevitable (that cannot be avoided).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Acknowlege.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Acknowlege" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "acknowledge" — the "d" before "-ge" must not be dropped. It means to accept or admit the truth or existence of something; to confirm receipt of something. (स्वीकार करना)

◦ Spelling key: AC + KNOW + LEDGE (remember the word "knowledge" hidden inside it).

◦ Example: He acknowledged his mistake before the whole class.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Territory" (an area of land under a ruler or state) — correctly spelt: TERRI + TORY, double "r".

• "Excellence" (the quality of being outstanding) — correctly spelt: EX + CELL + ENCE, double "l".

• "Business" (commercial activity) — correctly spelt: BUSI + NESS (from "busy" + "ness").

NOTE

• Word family: acknowledge (verb), acknowledgement / acknowledgment (noun), acknowledged (adjective).

• Other frequently misspelt SSC words: knowledge, privilege, judgement, maintenance, occurrence, embarrass, committee, recommend.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Authentic
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. False.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Authentic" means genuine, real and reliable; of undisputed origin. Its antonym is "false", meaning not true, fake or counterfeit. (प्रामाणिक का विलोम — झूठा / नकली)

◦ Example: The museum displays an authentic Mughal sword, not a false replica.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Actual" (real, existing in fact) is a synonym, not an antonym — a classic distractor.

• Option 1 "Moderate" (average, not extreme) and Option 4 "Wise" (having good judgement) are unrelated to the idea of genuineness.

NOTE

• Synonyms of authentic: genuine, real, actual, bona fide, veritable, reliable, credible.

• Antonyms of authentic: false, fake, counterfeit, spurious, bogus, forged, apocryphal.

• Word family: authenticity (noun), authenticate (verb — to prove genuine).

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

Please tell me about the meeting ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. in a nutshell.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "in a nutshell" means in a few words; very briefly; in summary. (संक्षेप में)

◦ Correct: Please tell me about the meeting in a nutshell. (= give me a short summary of it)

• The image is of something compressed so tightly that it could fit inside a nutshell.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "in a stew" means in a state of anxiety or agitation.

• Option 3 "in a huff" means in an angry, offended mood ("She left the room in a huff").

• Option 4 "in a spin" means in a state of confusion or panic.

• None of these three fits a request for information about a meeting.

NOTE

• Idioms of brevity: "in a nutshell", "in brief", "to cut a long story short", "in short", "the long and the short of it".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Augmented Reality (AR) continues to develop and become more _________ among a wide range of applications.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. pervasive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Pervasive" means spreading widely throughout an area or a group of people; present everywhere. Since AR "continues to develop", it naturally becomes more widespread "among a wide range of applications". (व्यापक / सर्वव्यापी)

◦ Correct: Augmented Reality (AR) continues to develop and become more pervasive among a wide range of applications.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "rare" (uncommon) contradicts "continues to develop ... among a wide range of applications".

• Option 2 "amicable" (friendly, showing goodwill) is used of people and relations, not of technology.

• Option 3 "idealistic" (guided by ideals rather than practical considerations) does not suit a spreading technology.

NOTE

• Synonyms of pervasive: widespread, prevalent, ubiquitous, omnipresent, rife, extensive.

• Antonyms: rare, scarce, uncommon, limited, localised.

• Word family: pervade (verb — to spread through), pervasion (noun).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Aweful.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Aweful" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "awful" — when the suffix "-ful" is added to "awe", the final "e" is dropped. It means very bad, unpleasant or terrible. (भयानक / बहुत बुरा)

◦ Spelling key: AW + FUL (one "l", no "e").

◦ Example: The weather was awful throughout our trip.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Grammar" — correctly spelt; note it ends in "-ar", not "-er" (remember: "gram-mar", not "grammer").

• "Pleasant" — correctly spelt: PLEAS + ANT (from "please").

• "Familiar" — correctly spelt: FAMILI + AR, again ending in "-ar".

NOTE

• The suffix "-ful" always has one "l" as an adjective ending: beautiful, wonderful, careful, useful, awful. (As a separate word, "full" has two.)

• Note also the meaning difference: "awful" = terrible, whereas "awesome" = causing admiration/wonder, and "awe-inspiring" = filling one with awe.

question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence.

The handloom shop at the Ring Road has many kinds of bags, such as paper, leather, cloth and cannvas.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Cannvas.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Cannvas" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "canvas" — with a single "n" and a single "s". It means a strong, coarse cloth used for making bags, tents, sails and for painting on. (कैनवास / मोटा कपड़ा)

◦ Spelling key: CAN + VAS.

◦ Example: The artist stretched a fresh canvas on the frame.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Paper", "Leather" and "Cloth" in the sentence are all spelt correctly.

• Note the pair canvas (the cloth — noun) vs canvass (with double "s" — a verb meaning to solicit votes or opinions): "Party workers went out to canvass for votes."

NOTE

• Other commonly misspelt fabric/material words: muslin, khadi, corduroy, chiffon, velvet, denim, satin, linen.

• Rule of thumb for such items: read every option aloud, syllable by syllable, and check for wrongly doubled consonants — the most frequent trick in SSC spelling questions.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

A/An ________ fellow cannot become an ideal teacher.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. idle.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence carries a negative sense — "cannot become an ideal teacher" — so the blank must take a word with a negative quality.

• "Idle" means lazy; not working; avoiding work. A lazy person naturally cannot become an ideal teacher. (आलसी / निठल्ला)

◦ Correct: An idle fellow cannot become an ideal teacher.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "bright", 3 "intelligent" and 4 "honest" are all positive qualities; each of them would actually help a person become a good teacher, so they contradict the negative verb "cannot become".

• The "A/An" in the question is a deliberate hint that the answer may begin with either a consonant or a vowel sound — here "an idle fellow".

NOTE

• Do not confuse "idle" (lazy, unemployed, unused) with "idol" (an image of a deity; a person greatly admired) — they are near-homophones and a favourite SSC trap.

• Synonyms of idle: lazy, indolent, slothful, lethargic, inactive. Antonyms: industrious, diligent, hardworking, assiduous.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

I considered Geography as an easier subject.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. an easy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The comparative degree ("easier") can be used only when a comparison with another thing is made, normally with "than". Here there is no "than" clause and no second item for comparison, so the comparative is wrong.

• The sentence merely states an opinion about Geography, so the positive degree "easy" with the article "an" is correct.

◦ Correct: I considered Geography as an easy subject.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "the easy" and Option 2 "the easier" wrongly use the definite article "the" before a general, unidentified description.

• Option 3 "an easiest" is doubly wrong — the superlative always takes "the" ("the easiest"), never "an".

NOTE

• Degrees of comparison: easy (positive) – easier (comparative, used with "than") – the easiest (superlative, used with "the").

• Articles: use "a/an" for a non-specific singular countable noun and "the" for something specific or already identified. Also remember the structure "consider/regard someone as something".

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The most common hazard in forests is forest fire. Forest fires are as old as the forests themselves. They pose a 1.________ not only to the forest wealth but also to the entire regime to fauna and flora seriously disturbing the biodiversity and the ecology and environment of a region. During summer, when there is no rain for months, the forests 2.________ littered with dry senescent leaves and twinges, which could burst into flames ignited by the slightest spark. The Himalayan forests, particularly, Garhwal Himalayas have been burning 3.________ during the last few summers, with colossal loss of vegetation cover of that region. The youngest mountain ranges of the Himalayas are the most 4.________ stretches of the world susceptible to forest fires. The forests of the Western are more 5.________ vulnerable to forest fires as compared to those in the Eastern Himalayas. This is because forests of the Eastern Himalayas grow in high rain density.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. threat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage says forest fires "pose a 1.________ not only to the forest wealth but also to the entire regime to fauna and flora". The verb "pose" collocates fixedly with "a threat" — "to pose a threat (to something)" means to be a source of danger to it. (खतरा)

◦ Correct: They pose a threat not only to the forest wealth but also to the entire regime to fauna and flora ...

• The whole passage describes forest fire as a "hazard" causing "colossal loss", which confirms the sense of danger.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "mercy" (compassion) is contextually opposite to a hazard.

• Option 2 "trend" (a general direction of change) does not go with "pose ... to the forest wealth".

• Option 3 "failure" is not something that can be "posed to" forest wealth and flora.

NOTE

• Learn the collocations of "pose": pose a threat, pose a danger, pose a risk, pose a challenge, pose a problem, pose a question.

• Synonyms of threat: danger, menace, peril, hazard, risk.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The most common hazard in forests is forest fire. Forest fires are as old as the forests themselves. They pose a 1.________ not only to the forest wealth but also to the entire regime to fauna and flora seriously disturbing the biodiversity and the ecology and environment of a region. During summer, when there is no rain for months, the forests 2.________ littered with dry senescent leaves and twinges, which could burst into flames ignited by the slightest spark. The Himalayan forests, particularly, Garhwal Himalayas have been burning 3.________ during the last few summers, with colossal loss of vegetation cover of that region. The youngest mountain ranges of the Himalayas are the most 4.________ stretches of the world susceptible to forest fires. The forests of the Western are more 5.________ vulnerable to forest fires as compared to those in the Eastern Himalayas. This is because forests of the Eastern Himalayas grow in high rain density.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. become.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs a linking verb joining the subject "the forests" to the adjectival phrase "littered with dry senescent leaves and twinges". "Become" is a linking verb showing a change of state, which fits the seasonal change described ("During summer, when there is no rain for months"). (बन जाना)

◦ Correct: During summer ... the forests become littered with dry senescent leaves and twinges ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "keep" would need a different structure and does not convey the change caused by the dry season.

• Option 2 "build" is transitive here and cannot take "littered" as a complement.

• Option 4 "drive littered" is ungrammatical and meaningless.

NOTE

• Common linking (copular) verbs that take an adjective/participial complement: be, become, seem, appear, look, feel, grow, turn, get, remain, stay.

• Note the passage's own spelling "twinges" (for "twigs") has been kept as printed.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The most common hazard in forests is forest fire. Forest fires are as old as the forests themselves. They pose a 1.________ not only to the forest wealth but also to the entire regime to fauna and flora seriously disturbing the biodiversity and the ecology and environment of a region. During summer, when there is no rain for months, the forests 2.________ littered with dry senescent leaves and twinges, which could burst into flames ignited by the slightest spark. The Himalayan forests, particularly, Garhwal Himalayas have been burning 3.________ during the last few summers, with colossal loss of vegetation cover of that region. The youngest mountain ranges of the Himalayas are the most 4.________ stretches of the world susceptible to forest fires. The forests of the Western are more 5.________ vulnerable to forest fires as compared to those in the Eastern Himalayas. This is because forests of the Eastern Himalayas grow in high rain density.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. regularly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The clause is "The Himalayan forests, particularly, Garhwal Himalayas have been burning 3.________ during the last few summers". The present perfect continuous with "during the last few summers" indicates an action repeated again and again over a period, so the adverb of frequency "regularly" (at regular/frequent intervals) fits best. (नियमित रूप से)

◦ Correct: ... have been burning regularly during the last few summers, with colossal loss of vegetation cover of that region.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "rarely" (seldom) contradicts "colossal loss of vegetation cover" repeated over several summers.

• Option 3 "badly" describes manner/degree rather than the repetition that "during the last few summers" demands, and it also weakens the link with "last few summers".

• Option 4 "enough" is not used as an adverb of frequency and gives no sensible meaning here.

NOTE

• Adverbs of frequency ranked: always > usually > regularly/frequently > often > sometimes > occasionally > seldom/rarely > never.

• The present perfect continuous (have/has been + V-ing) shows an action that began in the past and is still continuing or repeating.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The most common hazard in forests is forest fire. Forest fires are as old as the forests themselves. They pose a 1.________ not only to the forest wealth but also to the entire regime to fauna and flora seriously disturbing the biodiversity and the ecology and environment of a region. During summer, when there is no rain for months, the forests 2.________ littered with dry senescent leaves and twinges, which could burst into flames ignited by the slightest spark. The Himalayan forests, particularly, Garhwal Himalayas have been burning 3.________ during the last few summers, with colossal loss of vegetation cover of that region. The youngest mountain ranges of the Himalayas are the most 4.________ stretches of the world susceptible to forest fires. The forests of the Western are more 5.________ vulnerable to forest fires as compared to those in the Eastern Himalayas. This is because forests of the Eastern Himalayas grow in high rain density.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. vulnerable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Vulnerable" means exposed to harm or damage; easily hurt or attacked. The sentence says the youngest mountain ranges of the Himalayas are "the most ________ stretches of the world susceptible to forest fires", so the blank must repeat the idea of being open to danger. (असुरक्षित / संवेदनशील)

◦ Correct: The youngest mountain ranges of the Himalayas are the most vulnerable stretches of the world susceptible to forest fires.

• The word "vulnerable" also reappears in the next sentence of the passage ("more ______ vulnerable to forest fires"), confirming the theme.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "outrageous" (shockingly bad or offensive) describes behaviour, not terrain.

• Option 3 "greasy" (covered with grease/oil) is irrelevant to mountain stretches.

• Option 4 "mysterious" (difficult to understand or explain) does not connect with susceptibility to fire.

NOTE

• Synonyms of vulnerable: susceptible, exposed, defenceless, unprotected, at risk, sensitive.

• Antonyms: invulnerable, immune, protected, secure, resistant.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The most common hazard in forests is forest fire. Forest fires are as old as the forests themselves. They pose a 1.________ not only to the forest wealth but also to the entire regime to fauna and flora seriously disturbing the biodiversity and the ecology and environment of a region. During summer, when there is no rain for months, the forests 2.________ littered with dry senescent leaves and twinges, which could burst into flames ignited by the slightest spark. The Himalayan forests, particularly, Garhwal Himalayas have been burning 3.________ during the last few summers, with colossal loss of vegetation cover of that region. The youngest mountain ranges of the Himalayas are the most 4.________ stretches of the world susceptible to forest fires. The forests of the Western are more 5.________ vulnerable to forest fires as compared to those in the Eastern Himalayas. This is because forests of the Eastern Himalayas grow in high rain density.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. frequently.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence compares two regions: "The forests of the Western are more 5.________ vulnerable to forest fires as compared to those in the Eastern Himalayas." The adverb must express how often the Western forests are affected — "frequently" (often, again and again) fits the comparison of fire incidence. (बार-बार / अक्सर)

◦ Correct: The forests of the Western are more frequently vulnerable to forest fires as compared to those in the Eastern Himalayas.

• The reason given in the next line — the Eastern Himalayas "grow in high rain density" — supports the idea that fires occur more often in the drier Western Himalayas.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "closely" (in a near or careful manner) does not describe the frequency of fires.

• Option 3 "deeply" refers to intensity/depth of feeling, not to how often something happens.

• Option 4 "barely" (hardly, scarcely) reverses the intended meaning of greater vulnerability.

NOTE

• "More + adverb/adjective ... as compared to / than" is the standard comparative structure.

• Synonyms of frequently: often, repeatedly, regularly, recurrently, time and again. Antonyms: rarely, seldom, infrequently.

question: What is the purpose of a savings account?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Earning interest on deposits.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The basic purpose of a "savings account" is to encourage saving by allowing the depositor to keep surplus money safely in a bank and earn interest on the deposit. (बचत खाता — जमा पर ब्याज अर्जित करना)

• Savings accounts pay a rate of interest fixed by the bank (deregulated by the RBI since 2011) and place certain limits on the number of withdrawals/transactions.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• A "current account" is the one meant for frequent day-to-day transactions (Option 3) and it normally pays no interest; it is used by businesses and firms.

• A mortgage loan (Option 1) is obtained from the loan department against property, not through a savings account.

• Paying bills online (Option 4) is only a facility available on many accounts, not the purpose of a savings account.

NOTE

• Types of bank deposit accounts: Savings, Current, Recurring Deposit (RD), Fixed/Term Deposit (FD).

• Under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY, 2014), zero-balance Basic Savings Bank Deposit Accounts (BSBDA) are opened for financial inclusion.

• Bank deposits are insured up to ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank by the DICGC.

question: According to the Census of India 2011, the female literacy rate was recorded as ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 65.46%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census of India 2011, the female literacy rate was 65.46%, while the male literacy rate was 82.14% and the overall literacy rate was 74.04%. (महिला साक्षरता दर — 65.46%)

• Literacy is measured for the population aged 7 years and above.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Kerala had the highest literacy rate (93.91%) and Bihar the lowest (61.80%) in Census 2011.

• Kerala also recorded the highest female literacy, while Rajasthan recorded the lowest female literacy.

• The sex ratio in Census 2011 was 943 females per 1000 males; the child sex ratio (0–6 years) was 919.

NOTE

• Census 2011 was the 15th National Census of India and the 7th after Independence; its slogan was "Our Census, Our Future".

• The first census in India was conducted in 1872 under Lord Mayo, and the first complete/synchronous census in 1881 under Lord Ripon.

question: Which of the following crops is most suitable for black soil?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cotton.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Black soil" is the most suitable soil for growing cotton, which is why it is popularly called "black cotton soil" or "regur soil". (काली मिट्टी — कपास)

• It is formed from the weathering of basaltic lava (Deccan Trap) rocks and is rich in lime, iron, magnesia, alumina, calcium carbonate and potash, but poor in nitrogen, phosphorus and organic matter.

• Its high clay content gives it a great moisture-retaining capacity, which suits cotton, a crop that needs steady moisture in the dry season.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Black soil is found mainly in Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Chhattisgarh, parts of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Tamil Nadu — the Deccan plateau region.

• It develops deep cracks in summer, which help in aeration ("self-ploughing" soil), and becomes sticky when wet.

• Other crops grown on black soil: sugarcane, jowar, wheat, linseed, tobacco and oilseeds.

NOTE

• Major soil types of India: Alluvial (most widespread and fertile, Indo-Gangetic plains), Black/Regur, Red and Yellow, Laterite, Arid/Desert, Forest/Mountain and Saline/Alkaline.

question: In India, the ‘Aus’, ‘Aman’ and ‘Boro’ terms are associated with which crop from the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Paddy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Aus", "Aman" and "Boro" are the three seasonal crops of paddy (rice) grown in West Bengal, Assam, Odisha and Bangladesh. (धान की तीन फसलें)

◦ Aus — the autumn rice, sown around March–April and harvested in June–July.

◦ Aman — the winter rice, the main kharif crop, sown in June–July and harvested in November–December (the largest of the three).

◦ Boro — the summer/spring rice, grown mostly under irrigation from November–December to March–April.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Rice is a kharif crop needing high temperature (above 25°C), high humidity and rainfall above 100 cm (or assured irrigation).

• West Bengal is the largest rice-producing state of India; Uttar Pradesh and Punjab follow.

• India is the world's second-largest producer of rice after China and among the largest exporters of rice.

NOTE

• Cropping seasons in India: Kharif (sown with the onset of the monsoon, June–July; harvested Sept–Oct — rice, maize, cotton, jowar, bajra), Rabi (sown Oct–Dec; harvested April–June — wheat, gram, mustard, barley) and Zaid (short summer season — watermelon, cucumber, muskmelon, fodder).

question: The President of India conferred the Padma Shri award to Gurcharan Singh for his distinguished service in the field of ______________ in 2023.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cricket.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Gurcharan Singh, the veteran cricket coach from Delhi, was conferred the Padma Shri in 2023 for his distinguished service in the field of sports — cricket. (गुरचरण सिंह — क्रिकेट कोच, पद्म श्री 2023)

• He is one of India's most respected coaches and a Dronacharya Award winner, who coached and mentored many international cricketers.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Padma Awards — Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri — are among the highest civilian honours of India, announced every year on the eve of Republic Day and conferred by the President of India.

• Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian award of India (after the Bharat Ratna, Padma Vibhushan and Padma Bhushan).

• The Padma Awards were instituted in 1954.

NOTE

• Sports honours of India: Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award (highest sporting honour), Arjuna Award (outstanding performance), Dronacharya Award (coaches) and Dhyan Chand Award (lifetime achievement).

question: Who moved the resolution proposing that the National Flag of India be a ‘horizontal tricolour of saffron, white and dark green in equal proportion’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jawaharlal Nehru.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru moved the resolution in the Constituent Assembly on 22 July 1947 proposing that the National Flag of India be a "horizontal tricolour of deep saffron (kesari), white and dark green in equal proportion", with the Ashoka Chakra in navy blue at the centre of the white band. (राष्ट्रीय ध्वज संबंधी प्रस्ताव — जवाहरलाल नेहरू)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Ashoka Chakra has 24 spokes and is taken from the Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath; it replaced the charkha (spinning wheel) of the earlier Swaraj flag.

• The ratio of the width to the length of the flag is 2:3.

• The design of the flag is credited to Pingali Venkayya of Andhra Pradesh.

• Saffron stands for courage and sacrifice, white for truth and peace, and green for faith, fertility and prosperity.

NOTE

• The National Emblem (Lion Capital of Sarnath) was adopted on 26 January 1950; the National Anthem "Jana Gana Mana" was adopted on 24 January 1950 by the Constituent Assembly.

• Display of the flag is governed by the Flag Code of India, 2002 and the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971.

question: In which of the following States was the first Janjatiya Khel Mahotsav held?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odisha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first Janjatiya Khel Mahotsav (National Tribal Games / Tribal Sports Meet) was held in Odisha, at Bhubaneswar (Kalinga Stadium) in June 2023. (पहला जनजातीय खेल महोत्सव — ओडिशा)

• It was organised by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs in association with the state government and the sports authorities to give a national platform to tribal sporting talent.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Thousands of tribal athletes from across the country participated in disciplines such as athletics, football, archery, volleyball, kabaddi and traditional tribal games.

• Odisha has emerged as a major sporting hub of India, hosting the Hockey World Cup (2018 and 2023) and sponsoring the Indian hockey teams.

• Odisha has the largest number of Scheduled Tribes communities (62) among Indian states.

NOTE

• Related tribal initiatives: Janjatiya Gaurav Divas (15 November, birth anniversary of Birsa Munda), Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS), Van Dhan Vikas Kendras and the TRIFED marketing platform "Tribes India".

question: Identify the Indian singer who sang the song ‘Ae mere watan ke logon jara akhon mein bharlo paani…’ before the first Prime Minister of India, Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lata Mangeshkar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The patriotic song "Ae Mere Watan Ke Logon" was sung by Lata Mangeshkar on 27 January 1963 at the National Stadium, Delhi, in the presence of the first Prime Minister Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, who is famously said to have been moved to tears. (लता मंगेशकर)

• The song was written by Kavi Pradeep and composed by C. Ramchandra, as a tribute to the soldiers who died in the Indo-China War of 1962.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Lata Mangeshkar (1929–2022), known as the "Nightingale of India" and "Melody Queen", recorded songs in over 36 languages across a career of more than seven decades.

• She was awarded the Bharat Ratna (2001), the Padma Bhushan (1969), the Padma Vibhushan (1999) and the Dadasaheb Phalke Award (1989).

NOTE

• Other famous patriotic songs: "Sare Jahan Se Achha" (Muhammad Iqbal), "Vande Mataram" (Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay), "Jhanda Uncha Rahe Hamara" (Shyamlal Gupta 'Parshad') and "Kadam Kadam Badhaye Ja" (INA marching song).

question: Which regulatory body in India is responsible for overseeing and regulating Micro Finance Institutions?
option_1: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
option_2: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)
option_4: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)
solution_text:
The correct answer is Reserve Bank of India (RBI).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the regulatory body responsible for overseeing and regulating Micro Finance Institutions (MFIs) in India, which are registered as NBFC-MFIs (Non-Banking Financial Company – Micro Finance Institutions). (भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक — सूक्ष्म वित्त संस्थाओं का नियामक)

• The RBI issued the Regulatory Framework for Microfinance Loans, 2022, which defines a microfinance loan as a collateral-free loan to a household with annual income up to ₹3 lakh.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• SEBI (1988; statutory in 1992) regulates the securities/capital market.

• SIDBI (1990) is the principal financial institution for the promotion and financing of MSMEs.

• NABARD (1982) is the apex institution for agriculture and rural development and refinances rural credit; it supports but does not regulate MFIs.

NOTE

• The Reserve Bank of India was established on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934, on the recommendation of the Hilton Young Commission, and was nationalised in 1949. Its first Governor was Sir Osborne Smith and the first Indian Governor was C. D. Deshmukh.

• Other regulators: IRDAI (insurance), PFRDA (pensions), TRAI (telecom).

question: Who among the following was the viceroy of India at the time of India’s independence from colonial rule on 15 August 1947?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Mountbatten.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Lord Louis Mountbatten was the Viceroy of India at the time of India's independence on 15 August 1947. He was the last Viceroy of British India (March–August 1947) and then became the first Governor-General of independent India (1947–48). (लॉर्ड माउंटबेटन)

• The Mountbatten Plan (3 June 1947) proposed the partition of India into India and Pakistan; it was given effect by the Indian Independence Act, 1947 passed by the British Parliament on 18 July 1947.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Lord Wavell (1943–47) — preceded Mountbatten; associated with the Wavell Plan and the Shimla Conference (1945) and the Cabinet Mission (1946).

• Lord Linlithgow (1936–43) — August Offer (1940), Cripps Mission (1942) and the Quit India Movement (1942).

• Lord Willingdon (1931–36) — the Second and Third Round Table Conferences, the Communal Award (1932) and the Poona Pact (1932).

NOTE

• C. Rajagopalachari was the first and only Indian Governor-General of India (1948–1950).

• Lord Canning was the last Governor-General and the first Viceroy of India (after the Government of India Act, 1858).

question: Which of the following is the legislative organ of the Union Government?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Parliament.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Parliament is the legislative organ (law-making body) of the Union Government of India. Under Article 79, the Parliament of India consists of the President, the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) and the Lok Sabha (House of the People). (संसद — संघ सरकार का विधायी अंग)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The three organs of government are the Legislature (makes laws), the Executive (implements laws) and the Judiciary (interprets laws) — the basis of the doctrine of separation of powers.

• The Cabinet and the Executive (President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers) form the executive organ; the Supreme Court heads the judiciary.

• Lok Sabha: maximum strength 550 (530 states + 20 UTs); Rajya Sabha: maximum strength 250 (238 elected + 12 nominated).

NOTE

• Lok Sabha members are directly elected for 5 years; Rajya Sabha is a permanent house that is never dissolved, with one-third of its members retiring every two years and a term of six years.

• A Money Bill (Article 110) can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, with the prior recommendation of the President.

question: Due to rapid urbanisation, the human lifestyle has changed severely; obesity is a major health issue in such condition. Which of the following is a reason for obesity?
option_2: Excessive intake of high calorie foods
option_4: Lack of vitamins in regular diet
solution_text:
The correct answer is Excessive intake of high calorie foods.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Obesity is caused mainly by an energy imbalance — when the calories consumed exceed the calories burnt. Hence excessive intake of high-calorie foods (fats, sugars, fried and junk food) along with a sedentary lifestyle is a leading cause. (मोटापा — अधिक कैलोरी वाले भोजन का सेवन)

• The surplus energy is stored in the body as fat (adipose tissue).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 — drinking water adds no calories, so it does not cause obesity.

• Options 3 and 4 — lack of protein causes kwashiorkor/marasmus (protein-energy malnutrition) and lack of vitamins causes deficiency diseases (e.g., scurvy, beriberi, rickets), not obesity.

NOTE

• Obesity is measured by the Body Mass Index (BMI) = weight (kg) / height² (m²). WHO classification: underweight <18.5, normal 18.5–24.9, overweight 25–29.9, obese ≥30.

• Obesity raises the risk of type-2 diabetes, hypertension, heart disease, stroke and certain cancers.

• Energy value: 1 g carbohydrate ≈ 4 kcal, 1 g protein ≈ 4 kcal, 1 g fat ≈ 9 kcal.

question: Who won the Best Playback Singer (Male) award in the 68th Filmfare Awards 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arijit Singh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Arijit Singh won the Best Playback Singer (Male) award at the 68th Filmfare Awards, 2023, for the song "Kesariya" from the film "Brahmāstra: Part One – Shiva". (अरिजीत सिंह)

• The 68th Filmfare Awards ceremony was held in April 2023.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• At the same ceremony, "Gangubai Kathiawadi" swept the major awards — Best Film, Best Director (Sanjay Leela Bhansali) and Best Actress (Alia Bhatt); Rajkummar Rao won Best Actor for "Badhaai Do".

• Arijit Singh is among the most awarded playback singers of recent times, with hits such as "Tum Hi Ho", "Channa Mereya", "Ae Dil Hai Mushkil" and "Kesariya".

NOTE

• The Filmfare Awards were instituted in 1954 and are given by The Times Group; the trophy is popularly called the "Black Lady".

• The National Film Awards are the highest official film honours of India, and the Dadasaheb Phalke Award is the highest award in Indian cinema.

question: Where was Shree Narayana Dharma Paripalana Yogam founded?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Shree Narayana Dharma Paripalana (SNDP) Yogam" was founded in Kerala in 1903 (at Aruvippuram, near Thiruvananthapuram) under the inspiration of the great social reformer and saint Sree Narayana Guru, with Dr Padmanabhan Palpu and the poet Kumaran Asan playing leading roles. (एसएनडीपी योगम — केरल)

• It worked for the upliftment of the Ezhava community and against caste discrimination and untouchability in Kerala.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Sree Narayana Guru gave the famous message "One Caste, One Religion, One God for Man" (Oru Jathi, Oru Matham, Oru Daivam Manushyanu).

• He consecrated a Shiva temple at Aruvippuram in 1888, defying the rule that only Brahmins could install idols.

• The Vaikom Satyagraha (1924–25) in Travancore, supported by Gandhiji and Periyar, demanded temple-entry rights for the depressed classes.

NOTE

• Other social reform movements: Brahmo Samaj (Raja Ram Mohan Roy, 1828), Arya Samaj (Dayanand Saraswati, 1875), Prarthana Samaj (Atmaram Pandurang, 1867), Satyashodhak Samaj (Jyotiba Phule, 1873) and the Self-Respect Movement (E. V. Ramasamy 'Periyar', 1925).

question: Who is the renowned kathak dancer, student of ‘Pandit Birju Maharaj’ and also served as an officer with Indian Audit and Accounts Services?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shovana Narayan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Shovana Narayan is a renowned Kathak dancer and a disciple of the legendary Pandit Birju Maharaj. She was also a career civil servant, serving as an officer of the Indian Audit and Accounts Service (IA&AS). (शोवना नारायण — कथक)

• She was awarded the Padma Shri (1992) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1999–2000).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Sonal Mansingh — celebrated Odissi and Bharatanatyam dancer, Padma Vibhushan awardee and a nominated member of the Rajya Sabha.

• Guru Bipin Singh — the doyen of Manipuri dance.

• Padma Subrahmanyam — eminent Bharatanatyam dancer and researcher, known for reviving "Bharata Nrityam".

NOTE

• Kathak is the classical dance of North India (Uttar Pradesh), derived from "katha" (story); its main gharanas are Lucknow, Jaipur, Banaras and Raigarh.

• Other Kathak exponents: Pandit Birju Maharaj, Sitara Devi, Damayanti Joshi, Kumudini Lakhia and Uma Sharma.

question: Shama Bhate received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award-2021 (given in February 2023) for her contribution to which dance form of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Shama Bhate, the eminent dancer and choreographer from Pune, received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for 2021 (presented in February 2023) for her contribution to the Kathak dance form. (शमा भाटे — कथक)

• She is a disciple of Pandita Rohini Bhate and belongs to the Jaipur gharana tradition of Kathak.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi (SNA) was established in 1952/1953 and is India's national academy for music, dance and drama, functioning under the Ministry of Culture.

• Its highest honour is the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship (Akademi Ratna), limited to 40 living persons at a time; the Akademi Award (Akademi Puraskar) is given annually in various categories.

NOTE

• India's eight classical dance forms: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (Uttar Pradesh), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: Which of the following Indus Valley sites is now located in Pakistan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Harappa.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Harappa" is situated on the bank of the river Ravi in the Montgomery (Sahiwal) district of Punjab province, Pakistan. It was excavated by Daya Ram Sahni in 1921 and gave the civilization its name — the Harappan Civilization. (हड़प्पा — पाकिस्तान)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Lothal (Gujarat, on the Bhogavo river) — famous for the world's earliest known dockyard; excavated by S. R. Rao.

• Alamgirpur (Uttar Pradesh, on the Hindon river) — the easternmost site of the civilization.

• Kalibangan (Rajasthan, on the Ghaggar) — known for ploughed fields and fire altars; excavated by B. B. Lal and B. K. Thapar.

• Other sites in Pakistan: Mohenjo-daro (Sindh, on the Indus — excavated by R. D. Banerji, 1922), Chanhudaro and Sutkagendor.

NOTE

• The Indus Valley Civilization (c. 2500–1750 BCE) was a Bronze Age urban civilization known for grid-pattern town planning, burnt-brick houses, covered drainage, the Great Bath, granaries, standardised weights and an as-yet undeciphered script.

• Important Indian sites: Dholavira and Rakhigarhi (the largest site in India), Banawali, Ropar and Surkotada (horse bones).

question: In April 2023,Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty made history, becoming the first Indian men’s doubles pair to win a gold medal at the Badminton Asia Championships. Where was this championship held?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dubai.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In April 2023, the Indian pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty created history by becoming the first Indian men's doubles pair to win the gold medal at the Badminton Asia Championships, held in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. (दुबई — बैडमिंटन एशिया चैंपियनशिप 2023)

• They defeated the Malaysian pair Ong Yew Sin and Teo Ee Yi in the final.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The same pair also won gold at the Asian Games 2022 (held in Hangzhou in 2023) and became the world No. 1 men's doubles pair.

• They had earlier won gold at the Commonwealth Games 2022 (Birmingham) and the historic Thomas Cup 2022, when India won the title for the first time.

NOTE

• Indian badminton milestones: Prakash Padukone (first Indian to win the All England, 1980), Pullela Gopichand (All England, 2001), Saina Nehwal (first Indian woman Olympic medallist in badminton, 2012) and P. V. Sindhu (Olympic silver 2016, bronze 2021, World Champion 2019).

question: Which of the following states has introduced a dedicated Semiconductor Policy 2022-27 with a view to generate at least 2,00,000 new employment opportunities in the state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Gujarat became the first state in India to announce a dedicated Semiconductor Policy (2022–27), aiming to attract large investments in chip manufacturing and to generate at least 2,00,000 new employment opportunities in the state. (गुजरात — सेमीकंडक्टर नीति 2022-27)

• The policy offers capital and power subsidies, subsidised land and water in the proposed Dholera Semicon City (Dholera Special Investment Region).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The policy supports the Centre's "India Semiconductor Mission (ISM)" launched in 2021 with an outlay of about ₹76,000 crore, under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY).

• Major semiconductor projects in Gujarat include the Micron assembly and test plant at Sanand and the Tata Electronics–PSMC fab at Dholera.

NOTE

• A semiconductor is a material (like silicon or germanium) whose conductivity lies between that of a conductor and an insulator; chips made from it power all modern electronics.

• Global leaders in chip manufacturing: Taiwan (TSMC), South Korea (Samsung), the USA and China.

question: The classical dance style of Bharatanatyam belongs to the state of ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Bharatanatyam" is the classical dance style of the state of Tamil Nadu. It is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India and is based on the Natya Shastra of Bharat Muni. (भरतनाट्यम — तमिलनाडु)

• It was earlier performed in temples by the devadasis and was known as "Sadir" or "Dasiattam"; it was revived in the 20th century by Rukmini Devi Arundale (founder of Kalakshetra) and E. Krishna Iyer.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The name is often explained as BHA(bhava — expression) + RA(raga — melody) + TA(tala — rhythm) + NATYAM (dance).

• Famous exponents: Rukmini Devi Arundale, Balasaraswati, Yamini Krishnamurthy, Padma Subrahmanyam, Mallika Sarabhai and Alarmel Valli.

• The dance is accompanied by Carnatic music, with the nattuvanar conducting using cymbals (nattuvangam).

NOTE

• Classical dances and their states: Bharatanatyam – Tamil Nadu; Kathak – Uttar Pradesh; Kathakali & Mohiniyattam – Kerala; Kuchipudi – Andhra Pradesh; Odissi – Odisha; Manipuri – Manipur; Sattriya – Assam.

question: Which of the following peninsular rivers of India is a west flowing river?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Narmada.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Narmada" is a major west-flowing peninsular river of India. It rises from the Amarkantak plateau in Madhya Pradesh and flows westwards through a rift valley between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges, finally emptying into the Gulf of Khambhat (Arabian Sea). (नर्मदा — पश्चिम की ओर बहने वाली नदी)

• Because it flows through a rift valley (a fault trough), it forms an estuary, not a delta.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Kaveri, Godavari, Krishna and Mahanadi are east-flowing peninsular rivers that drain into the Bay of Bengal and form deltas.

• The Godavari is the largest peninsular river, called "Dakshina Ganga" (Vridha Ganga).

• The Tapi (Tapti) is the other major west-flowing river, also flowing through a rift valley into the Gulf of Khambhat.

NOTE

• Famous features on the Narmada: the Dhuandhar Falls and the Marble Rocks at Bhedaghat (Jabalpur), and the Sardar Sarovar Dam (Gujarat).

• Other west-flowing rivers: Mahi, Sabarmati, Luni, Periyar, Bharathappuzha and the Sharavathi (Jog Falls).

question: Which Articles of the Constitution of India deal with the Union and its territory?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Articles 1-4.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Part I of the Constitution of India, comprising Articles 1 to 4, deals with "The Union and its Territory". (अनुच्छेद 1-4 — संघ और उसका राज्यक्षेत्र)

◦ Article 1 — India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States.

◦ Article 2 — Parliament may admit or establish new States.

◦ Article 3 — Formation of new States and alteration of areas, boundaries or names of existing States.

◦ Article 4 — Laws made under Articles 2 and 3 are not deemed to be amendments under Article 368.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Articles 5–11 (Part II) — Citizenship.

• Articles 12–35 (Part III) — Fundamental Rights.

• Articles 36–51 (Part IV) — Directive Principles of State Policy.

• Articles 51A (Part IVA) — Fundamental Duties (added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976).

NOTE

• A Bill under Article 3 can be introduced only in Parliament with the prior recommendation of the President, and the President must refer it to the State Legislature concerned for its views (which are not binding).

• The States Reorganisation Act, 1956 reorganised states on a linguistic basis following the Fazl Ali Commission report.

question: ‘The Great Indian Novel’ is a satirical novel by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shashi Tharoor.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Great Indian Novel" (1989) is a satirical novel written by Shashi Tharoor. It recasts the story of the Mahabharata to narrate the events of 20th-century Indian history and politics, from the freedom struggle to the Emergency. (शशि थरूर)

• The title is a pun on the "Great American Novel" and on "Maha-bharata" ("maha" = great).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Shashi Tharoor is a diplomat-turned-politician (former Under-Secretary-General of the UN) and Member of Parliament; his other books include "An Era of Darkness", "Why I Am a Hindu", "India: From Midnight to the Millennium" and "The Paradoxical Prime Minister".

• Suryakant Tripathi 'Nirala' — a great Hindi poet of the Chhayavaad school ("Saroj Smriti", "Ram Ki Shakti Puja").

• R. K. Narayan — English novelist famous for creating Malgudi ("Swami and Friends", "The Guide", "The Man-Eater of Malgudi").

• Munshi Premchand — the "Upanyas Samrat" of Hindi/Urdu fiction ("Godaan", "Gaban", "Nirmala", "Karmabhoomi").

NOTE

• Other well-known Indian English novels: "Midnight's Children" (Salman Rushdie), "The God of Small Things" (Arundhati Roy), "A Suitable Boy" (Vikram Seth), "The White Tiger" (Aravind Adiga) and "The Inheritance of Loss" (Kiran Desai).

question: What is the systematic name of a colourless gas with a faint, ethereal odour called acetylene, widely used for welding?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ethyne.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Acetylene" is the common name of the gas whose systematic (IUPAC) name is "Ethyne", with the formula C₂H₂ (HC≡CH). It is the simplest alkyne, containing a carbon–carbon triple bond. (एथाइन — एसिटिलीन)

• It is a colourless gas with a faint ethereal odour (the garlic-like smell of commercial acetylene is due to impurities such as phosphine).

• Burnt with oxygen in an oxy-acetylene torch, it gives a flame of about 3300°C, which is used for welding and cutting metals.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Acetylene is prepared in the laboratory by the action of water on calcium carbide: CaC₂ + 2H₂O → C₂H₂ + Ca(OH)₂.

• It is also used for the artificial ripening of fruits (via ethylene-like action) and in the manufacture of plastics and synthetic rubber.

• Option 2 "Ethanoic anhydride" is (CH₃CO)₂O, Option 3 "Azoethane" is C₂H₅–N=N–C₂H₅, and Option 4 "Ethyl acetate" is CH₃COOC₂H₅ — an ester used as a solvent.

NOTE

• Homologous series suffixes: -ane for alkanes (single bond, CₙH₂ₙ₊₂), -ene for alkenes (double bond, CₙH₂ₙ) and -yne for alkynes (triple bond, CₙH₂ₙ₋₂).

• Common name vs IUPAC name: acetylene → ethyne; ethylene → ethene; marsh gas → methane; acetic acid → ethanoic acid; formic acid → methanoic acid.

question: Identify the correct pair of novel and its writer from the following.
option_2: <style> @font-face { font-family: 'Kiran';src: url('https://appxcontent.kaxa.in/fonts/Kiran.ttf') format('truetype');} </style>The White Tiger - Kiran Desai
solution_text:
The correct answer is Seven Summers - Mulk Raj Anand.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Seven Summers" (1951) is an autobiographical novel by Mulk Raj Anand, the first part of his projected seven-part series "The Seven Ages of Man". It describes the first seven years of the author's childhood. (सेवन समर्स — मुल्क राज आनंद)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The other three pairs are wrongly matched:

◦ "The White Tiger" was written by Aravind Adiga (Booker Prize, 2008), not Kiran Desai.

◦ "A Suitable Boy" was written by Vikram Seth, not Amitav Ghosh.

◦ "The Inheritance of Loss" was written by Kiran Desai (Booker Prize, 2006), not Aravind Adiga.

• Mulk Raj Anand (1905–2004) was one of the pioneers of Indian writing in English, famous for his social realism; his major works include "Untouchable" (1935), "Coolie" (1936), "Two Leaves and a Bud" and "The Village". He received the Padma Bhushan and the Sahitya Akademi Award.

NOTE

• Indian winners of the Booker Prize: Arundhati Roy ("The God of Small Things", 1997), Kiran Desai ("The Inheritance of Loss", 2006), Aravind Adiga ("The White Tiger", 2008), Salman Rushdie ("Midnight's Children", 1981) and V. S. Naipaul ("In a Free State", 1971). Geetanjali Shree won the International Booker Prize (2022) for "Tomb of Sand" (Ret Samadhi).
